title: Alert Rules and Alertmanager
intro: Good alerts wake people up only for things that need a human, right now. Bad alerts train people to ignore pages. Validating rules and managing silences are part of keeping the signal clean.

steps.prompt: Validate your alert rules file before loading it.
steps.explanation: All six rules parse and their PromQL is valid.
steps.why: A typo in one rule's expression can prevent the whole rule group from loading — meaning alerts you think exist silently don't. Run this in CI on every change to alert rules.

steps.prompt: Unit-test your alert rules against synthetic data to prove HighErrorRate actually fires when it should.
steps.explanation: promtool feeds fake time series into the rules and checks which alerts fire, and when.
steps.why: Syntax checking proves an alert is valid; tests prove it's correct. Without tests, the first time you learn an alert never fires is during the incident it should have caught.

steps.prompt: Check which alerts are firing right now in Alertmanager.
steps.fake_output:
Alertname       Starts At        Summary
HighErrorRate   10:02:11 UTC     Error rate above 5% for 10 minutes
DiskWillFillIn4h 09:40:00 UTC   /var on db01 fills in ~4h
steps.explanation: Two active alerts, with their summary annotations.
steps.why: Note 'DiskWillFillIn4h' — predictive alerts (using predict_linear) give you hours to act instead of paging at 100% full. Alert on symptoms users feel plus a few key predictive causes.

steps.prompt: You're doing planned maintenance on db01 for 2 hours. Silence its alerts so on-call isn't paged for expected noise.
steps.explanation: Alerts matching instance=db01 are muted for 2 hours; the silence ID is returned.
steps.why: Always use an expiring silence with a comment — never disable the alert rule itself. Permanent 'temporary' mutes are how real outages go unnoticed weeks later.

steps.prompt: Maintenance finished early. Remove the silence.
steps.explanation: Alerting for db01 is active again.
steps.why: Ending silences early restores coverage immediately rather than leaving a blind spot for the remaining window.
